newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agents arrest founder of weed buyers' club.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agents arrest founder of weed buyers' club.

text.p: The founder of a San Francisco club that said it sold marijuana to thousands of seriously ill people was arrested on Friday on drug charges, state officials said.

Dennis Peron, founder of the San Francisco Cannabis Buyers' Club and a longtime crusader for the legalisation of marijuana for the seriously ill, was arrested by state narcotics agents at his home in San Francisco, Matt Ross, a spokesman for California Attorney-General Dan Lungren, said.

Lungren's office announced on Friday that Peron was one of six alleged owners and operators of the Cannabis Buyers' Club indicted by an Alameda County grand jury on charges of conspiracy, possession of marijuana for sale and sale or transportation of marijuana. The indictment was handed up on Tuesday but was sealed until Friday.

Authorities were seeking to arrest the other five people indicted -- Peter Veilleux, Antonio Martinez, John Hudson, Elizabeth Moore and Adam Perry, Ross said. All six face a maximum sentence of five years and eight months in prison if convicted on all of the felony charges, he said.
Lungren's office said the indictment stemmed from a two-year investigation by several law enforcement agencies.
At a hearing in Oakland on Friday, Alameda County Superior Court Judge Ronald Sabraw ordered Peron released on his own recognisance until his arraignment next Tuesday.

The indictments follow an Aug. 4 raid by state narcotics agents on the San Francisco Cannabis Buyers' Club, which operated in defiance of the law. The club has been closed since then by a court order.
The Cannabis Buyers' Club said it supplied marijuana to about 12,000 clients who it said used the drug to ease suffering caused by AIDS, cancer and glaucoma.

But Lungren's office has accused the club of routinely selling marijuana to children and people with forged doctors' notes or with no medical excuse. It said state agents seized 150 pounds (68 kgs) of marijuana, $60,000 in cash and more than 400 marijuana plants. No arrests were made until now.

Peron's arrest came less than a month before Californians were due to vote on a proposal to make it legal for sick people to grow and smoke marijuana in the state. Peron was an early backer of the "medical marijuana" initiative.

San Francisco District Attorney Terence Hallinan and supporters of the medical marijuana initiative accused Lungren, a Republican who opposes the proposal, of having a political motive for ordering the crackdown on the Cannabis Buyers' Club.
"It is a clear abuse of prosecutorial power, of an indictment being used for political purposes to affect the outcome of an election," Hallinan told a news conference.
Dave Fratello, a spokesman for the campaign in favour of the medical marijuana initiative, accused Lungren of being prepared to do anything to defeat the initiative.
Ross said Hallinan's charge that the move was politically inspired was "not worthy of a response."

Earlier this month, Lungren took issue with "Doonesbury" comic strip episodes poking fun at the raid on the Cannabis Buyers' Club. He urged Universal Press Syndicate, which distributes Garry Trudeau's strip, and California newspapers to "pull the plug" on the strips, but they took no action.
